Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our discussion I pulled together a short mutual action plan focused on the evaluation sprint and the cost/unit checks we agreed we'd validate before the PO. Please see the attached checklist (MAP-Cost-Checklist-v2.xlsx) — it's intentionally minimal so we can iterate quickly during the pilot.

High-level asks from our side so we can finalize the MAP this week:
- confirmation of expected daily/peak QPS and typical prompt size (tokens)
- a short list of the top 10 templated prompts you plan to evaluate (these are the best candidates for prefix/KV caching)
- success criteria for the eval (latency p95 target, quality baseline — e.g., % exact-match or top-1 acceptance)
- procurement contact and any PO timing constraints

On the Redwood assumptions side (for cost modeling):
- tokens per call: we modeled 200–300 tokens per request as a baseline
- caching: prefix caching for templates, KV cache with 10k key TTL for session reuse
- batching/throughput: we'll test batching windows 20–50ms and measure p95 impact

Can you confirm the two items above and whether you want us to include an expected monthly token volume for the pilot? If yes, please share a best-effort volume range (low/likely/high).

I'm looping Rishi and Priyom here — Rishi will own the MAP milestones and Priyom will run the evaluation plan/benchmarks with your engineering team. Marissa will support any SRE/setup for the private pilot if needed.

Subject: Re: MAP: cost assumptions & evaluation sprint (timeline and checkpoints)

Thanks Lena — useful numbers. A couple of quick follow-ups and proposed checkpoints so we can lock the MAP this week: 

Quoted from Lena: "Peak QPS: ~18 (steady-state avg ~2–3); tokens per call: ~250; p95 < 350ms; reviewer acceptance >=85%"

Our assumptions and proposal for the MAP cost checks:
- Token model: we'll run a 2-week micro-pilot with three capacity points: low (5k tokens/day), mid (50k tokens/day), and high (500k tokens/day) to validate unit economics across scale.
- Caching: recommend enabling prefix (template) caching for the templated prompts you mentioned. In practice that lowers token usage by 15–40% depending on template hit rate. We'll instrument cache-hit metrics in the console so you can see tokens saved live.
- Batching window: start with 20ms batching for interactive flows; measure p95 impact. If p95 increases >30ms, we'll reduce batching. For throughput-heavy background jobs we can increase batching (50–100ms) to improve tokens/$ by ~12–22%.
- KV cache: retain per-session KV for 10k keys with a 24h TTL for the pilot. We'll include a toggle so SRE can adjust TTL in real time.

Proposed MAP milestones (owner / target):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize MAP doc and procurement review — Hannah/Rishi — target 5/3
- Week 1: engineering setup + sample prompt ingest — Priyom/Clarity eng — target 5/10
- Week 2: micro-pilot low/mid load runs and cost telemetry collection — Priyom/Marissa — target 5/17
- Week 3: run high-load validation and regression evals; produce token/$ report — Rishi/Clarity PM — target 5/24

A couple of asks for clarity (quick answers please so we can size infra):
1) Do you expect a high template hit rate (>=30%) for the templated flows? If yes, savings will be significant.
2) Any regulatory constraints on caching PII or patient identifiers? If so, we'll scope cache TTLs and encryption accordingly.

I can prepare a short pilot price estimate (breakdown tokens, infra, and engineering hours) once we have the expected template-hit and token-volume ranges.

—Rishi

Cost modeling notes (what we'll validate during the pilot):
- tokens per call baseline: 250 tokens (adjustable if Clarity shares sample prompts)
- expected template hit-rate: we'll instrument and report; assumed range 10–40% for modeling
- caching savings: estimate 15–40% tokens saved on templated flows at 30% hit rate
- batching trade-off: 20ms initial batching window for interactive flows; if p95 latency jumps >30ms we'll reduce window; throughput batch windows (50–100ms) for background jobs will be tested for cost efficiency
- pilot cap recommendation: recommend a $5k cap for the micro-pilot (covers infra + model usage at mid volume); we'll provide a line-item breakout in the MAP doc

Next steps: Hannah will send the pilot price estimate + MAP doc (attaching to HubSpot deal) by 5/5. Please confirm procurement contact if different from procurement@clarityhealth.com.
